title: 花 (Hana — Flowers on the Sumida River)
description: A beloved Meiji-era art song. Lyrics by 武島羽衣 (Takeshima Hagoromo, 1900), music by 滝廉太郎 (Taki Rentarō, 1900). Three verses celebrate the spring Sumida River: boatmen's oars scatter blossoms like snow; cherry trees speak at dawn; willows beckon at dusk; the embankment glows with brocade under a hazy moon. Literary Meiji vocabulary: のぼりくだり (going up and down), 見ずや (do you not see?), あけぼの (daybreak), たとふべき (what can compare to this?). A staple of Japanese elementary school music education.
